title: Squared-length ratio between adjacent roots in a string
statement: Let $I$ be finite, let $V,W$ be vector spaces over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field], and let $P:\mathrm{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ V\ W$ be a reduced crystallographic root pairing in the Mathlib sense: injective root and coroot families with a perfect bilinear pairing, root-coroot value $2$, simultaneous reflection permutations, integral root-coroot pairings, and no proportional roots except a root and its negative. Write $a_i=P.\mathrm{root}(i)$. Let $b:V\times V\to\mathbf Q$ be a symmetric bilinear form, positive definite in the sense that $b(x,x)>0$ for $x\ne0$, and invariant under each root reflection $s_i(x)=x-\langle x,P.\mathrm{coroot}(i)\rangle a_i$. Let $i,j,k\in I$ with $a_i,a_j$ linearly independent over $\mathbf Q$ and $a_k=a_i+a_j$. Put $p=P.\mathrm{chainBotCoeff}(i,j)$ and $q=P.\mathrm{chainTopCoeff}(i,j)$, the largest nonnegative integers with $a_j-pa_i$ and $a_j+qa_i$ roots. Then $$q\,b(a_k,a_k)=(p+1)b(a_j,a_j).$$

source.place: Appendix C, Section g, printed pp.621--622, table (180) and the four rank-two root diagrams, with the invariant inner product of C.19. Agent-formulated adjacent-root length identity read from these diagrams; Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, pp.508--509 motivates its use.

proof.text: Write $\alpha=a_i$, $\beta=a_j$, $\gamma=a_k=\alpha+\beta$, $A=b(\alpha,\alpha)$, $B=b(\beta,\beta)$, $D=b(\gamma,\gamma)$, and $t=p-q\in\mathbf Z$. All three roots are nonzero since their root-coroot values are $2$, so $A,B,D>0$. For any root $a_l$ and any $x$, set $c=\langle x,P.\mathrm{coroot}(l)\rangle$. Since $s_l(a_l)=-a_l$, invariance and bilinearity give $b(x,a_l)=b(x-ca_l,-a_l)=-b(x,a_l)+c b(a_l,a_l)$, hence $2b(x,a_l)=c b(a_l,a_l)$. This is the formula of C.20, obtained directly from the stated hypotheses.

source.place: Appendix C.19--C.20, printed p.611, and Section g, printed pp.621--622; agent algebraic verification of the adjacent-root identity.

proof.text: The endpoint-difference node gives $\langle\beta,P.\mathrm{coroot}(i)\rangle=t$, so step 1 implies $2b(\alpha,\beta)=tA$ and $D=B+(t+1)A$. The interval node applied at $z=1$ gives $q\ge1$, because $\gamma$ is a root. The length-bound node gives $p+q\le3$. Consequently $(p,q)$ is one of $(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,1),(1,2),(2,1)$.

source.place: Appendix C.19--C.20, printed p.611, and Section g, printed pp.621--622; agent algebraic verification of the adjacent-root identity.

proof.text: If $t=-1$ (the pairs $(0,1)$ and $(1,2)$), then $D=B$ and $q=p+1$, so $qD=(p+1)B$.

source.place: Appendix C.19--C.20, printed p.611, and Section g, printed pp.621--622; agent algebraic verification of the adjacent-root identity.

proof.text: For $(p,q)=(0,2)$ or $(0,3)$, one has $t=-q$ and $D=B-(q-1)A>0$, so $B>(q-1)A$. The integer $r=\langle\alpha,P.\mathrm{coroot}(j)\rangle$ satisfies $rB=2b(\alpha,\beta)=-qA$ by step 1. Thus $-2<r<0$: for $q=2$ use $B>A$, and for $q=3$ use $B>2A$. Hence $r=-1$ and $B=qA$. Substitution gives $D=A$ and therefore $qD=B=(p+1)B$.

source.place: Appendix C.19--C.20, printed p.611, and Section g, printed pp.621--622; agent algebraic verification of the adjacent-root identity.

proof.text: The remaining pairs are $(p,q)=(1,1)$ and $(2,1)$. Now $t=p-1$ and $D=B+pA$. The integer $u=\langle\alpha,P.\mathrm{coroot}(k)\rangle$ satisfies $uD=2b(\alpha,\gamma)=(p+1)A$ by step 1 and bilinearity. Since $A,B>0$ and $p=1$ or $2$, we have $0<u<2$ (for $p=1$, $D>A$; for $p=2$, $D>2A$). Thus $u=1$, whence $D=(p+1)A$ and $B=A$. It follows that $qD=D=(p+1)B$, completing all cases.
